q: 1. The gradual accumulation of amount by way of annual periodic deposits meant for replacement of the structure at end of its useful life is known as
explain: A sinking fund is built up through regular annual deposits (with compound interest) so that enough money accumulates to replace the structure when its life ends.

q: 2. The technique of finding fair price of an existing building or property is known as:
explain: Valuation is the process used to determine the fair present-day worth of an existing building or property, considering age, condition, and market factors.

q: 3. Evaluation of building is done based on
explain: Preliminary evaluation of a building's cost is typically calculated using the plinth area rate of similar structures in the locality.

q: 4. Which department looks after the execution and maintenance of water supply and sanitary works?
options: Department of Urban Development and Housing Construction
explain: The Department of Water Supply and Sewerage is specifically responsible for executing and maintaining water supply and sanitary infrastructure.

q: 5. The value of a property is the amount of money whose annual interest at the highest prevailing rate of interest will be equal to the net income from the property.
explain: This defines the capitalised value -- the principal sum which, if invested at the prevailing interest rate, would yield an annual interest equal to the property's net income.

q: 6. The sinking fund is
options: a part of the proceed in reserve for additional structure and modification
the sum of money to be paid to authorities by the tenants
the fund for rebuilding a structure when its economic life is over
raised to meet the maintenance costs of the structure before dismantling
explain: A sinking fund is specifically accumulated through periodic deposits to provide the capital needed to rebuild or replace a structure once its economic life ends.

q: 7. In Nepal, the weightage given to the fair market value and government land value during the valuation of land is
options: 70% fair market value and 30% governmental land value
30% fair market value and 70% governmental land value
50% fair market value and 50% governmental land value
40% fair market value and 60% governmental land value
explain: As per Nepalese valuation practice, land value is determined by giving equal weightage of 50% each to the fair market value and the government-fixed land value.

q: 8. The term 'valuation' in Civil Engineering is the process of estimating the potential ....... of an asset.
explain: Valuation in civil engineering essentially estimates the book value (the recorded/derived worth) of an asset based on its condition and remaining life.

q: 9. The life of teak wood doors and window is usually taken to be
explain: The average service life of high-quality teak wood joinery in buildings is estimated at 40 years before significant decay or structural replacement is required.

q: 10. Valuation is done for
explain: The primary goal of valuation is to find the actual present value of the property in its current condition and market context.

q: 11. The usual annual repair and maintenance cost of building is
explain: The annual repair and maintenance cost of a building is conventionally taken as 10% of the gross income derived from the property, for valuation purposes.

q: 12. Which department looks after the execution and maintenance of water supply and sanitary works?
explain: In the traditional government departmental structure referenced here, the Public Works Department is responsible for executing and maintaining water supply and sanitary works.

q: 13. If the payment of annuity beings after some years in future, it is known as
explain: When the first annuity payment begins only after a lapse of some years in the future rather than immediately, it is termed a delayed annuity.

q: 14. Annual periodic payments made for repayment of capital invested is known as:
explain: Annuity is defined as the annual periodic payment made towards repayment of an invested capital sum.

q: 15. The average annual rate of return is expressed in
explain: The average annual rate of return on an investment is conventionally expressed as a percentage.

q: 16. The value of the property or structures become less by its becoming out of date in style is known as
explain: Obsolescence is the loss in value due to changes in design, technology, or demand, making the property 'outdated'.

q: 17. The value of the property (without being dismentaled) at the end of the useful life period is known as
explain: Salvage value is the value of an asset at the end of its utility without being broken up. (Note: Question text says 'salvation' which is a typo for 'salvage').

q: 18. The annual periodic payments made for the repayment of the capital invested is known as
explain: An annuity is a fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, often used to repay capital over a period of time.

q: 19. The net annual letting out value of a property, which is obtained after deducting the amount of yearly repairs from the gross income, is known as
explain: Rateable value is used by local authorities to calculate taxes, determined by deducting outgoings from gross rent.

q: 20. The gradual accumulations of amount by way of annual periodic deposits which is meant for the replacement of the structure at the end of its useful life period is known as
explain: A sinking fund is created by setting aside a specific sum annually so that the accumulated amount can replace the asset at the end of its life.

q: 21. The value of the dismentalled material less the cost of dismentalling is called
explain: Scrap value is the worth of the materials (bricks, steel, timber) after the building has been demolished.

q: 22. Original cost of property minus depreciation is
explain: Book value is defined as the original cost of a property minus the accumulated depreciation charged over its life.

q: 23. The value of a structure un-dismantled at the end of utility period is its
explain: Salvage value is the value of a structure as it stands, without being dismantled, at the end of its useful life.

q: 24. The valuation of a building depends upon
explain: The valuation of a building is influenced jointly by its structural durability, its size/shape/type, and the quality of materials used in construction -- all these factors together.

q: 25. The gradual reduction in value with age of a property is known as
explain: Depreciation is the standard term for the gradual reduction in a property's value that occurs with age and use.

q: 26. The valuation of a property is done when
options: owner of the property wants to sell it
municipal tax, wealth tax, estate duty, etc. have to be fixed
insurance of the property has to be done
explain: Valuation of property is required for multiple purposes: when selling it, when fixing municipal/wealth taxes or estate duty, and when arranging insurance -- so all listed reasons apply.

q: 27. The set annual letting out value of a property, which is obtained after deducting the amount of yearly repairs from the gross income, is known as
explain: Rateable value is the net annual letting value of a property after deducting the estimated annual repair/maintenance cost from the gross income, and is used as the basis for taxation.

q: 28. The value of the property (without being dismantled) at the end of the useful life period is
explain: Salvage value is the value of a property left intact (not dismantled) at the end of its useful life.

q: 29. Salvage value of any structure is
explain: Salvage value is the value of a property at the end of its utility period without being dismantled, which is typically higher than scrap value (value of dismantled materials).

q: 30. The amount of capital from required to be invested to receive a net annual income as an annuity of Rs. 1 /- at certain rate of interest is called
explain: Year's Purchase (YP) is the capital sum required to be invested to receive an annuity of Re 1.00 at a given rate of interest.

q: 31. Total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than ........ of the capital cost
explain: As per standard maintenance norms, total annual/special repair expenditure is limited to about 2.5% of the building's capital cost.

q: 32. The sinking fund is:
options: a part of the proceed in reserve for additional structure and modification
the sum of money to be paid to authorities by the tenants
the fund for rebuilding structure its economic life is over
raised to meet the maintenance costs of the structure before dismantling
explain: A sinking fund is a fund created by setting aside annual installments so that at the end of the utility period, the accumulated amount is enough to replace the structure.

q: 33. In a linear depreciation method of property valuation depreciation is imposed on costs related to:
explain: Land does not depreciate; depreciation is applied to the building structure which has a finite life.

q: 34. Annual rent is generally fixed at:
explain: Annual rent is typically estimated between 5% and 10% of the capitalized value of the building.

q: 35. Which of following is corrected?
explain: Salvage value (value of the structure intact at the end of its life) is generally greater than scrap value (value of dismantled/broken-down material), since dismantling reduces the material's usability and value.

q: 36. The total cost construction including cost of land is termed as
explain: Capital cost is defined as the total cost of a project, including both the cost of construction and the cost of the land on which it stands.
